hero.headline: Record any tab. Transcribe the lyrics. Ship the song.
hero.sub: TabTune Studio grabs the audio playing in your browser tab, hands it to Gemini for a timestamped lyric sheet, and lets you sing along in a live karaoke view — without muting your speakers, without leaving the tab.
hero.note: Free and open install while the Web Store listing is in review.

features.title: Capture the tab, not the room
features.body: Tab audio is routed through an AudioContext, so your speakers stay unmuted and no microphone hiss gets in. Choose WebM / Opus at up to 320 kbps, or WAV PCM 16-bit for FL Studio, Ableton and Logic.

features.title: A countdown that waits for you
features.body: Pick 0, 3, 5 or 10 seconds before capture starts. That is your window to switch to the music tab and hit play, so the take begins at bar one instead of halfway through the second verse.

features.title: Take memory
features.body: Finished takes are written to IndexedDB. Close the popup, close the browser, come back tomorrow — the last ten takes are still there, and the newest one reloads itself with a note saying what it recovered.

features.title: Gemini transcription, tuned for Bongo
features.body: Send the audio to Gemini and get back synchronised .lrc lines. The prompt is written for Kiswahili, Sheng and code-switched verses, and it can detect the language on its own.

features.title: Karaoke view and a one-key stamper
features.body: Play the take and the lines light up and scroll with it. Off by a beat? Put the cursor on the line and press Ctrl + T — the exact [mm:ss.xx] is stamped where your cursor is.

features.title: One bundle, everything in it
features.body: Export a .zip with the pristine audio, the synced .lrc, a clean .txt of the words and an info sheet with duration, bitrate and capture time. Or grab the .lrc on its own.

steps.title: Open the tab that is playing
steps.body: YouTube, SoundCloud, Spotify Web, Beatstars, a local player — anything making sound in a tab.

steps.title: Hit record, take the countdown
steps.body: Alt + Shift + R works from anywhere. The countdown gives you time to reach the tab and press play.

steps.title: Let Gemini write the timestamps
steps.body: Or pull existing synced lyrics from LRCLIB. Both land in the same editor.

steps.title: Play it back, nudge, export
steps.body: Watch the karaoke view, stamp any line that drifts, then export the bundle.

privacy.title: Your keys never leave your browser
privacy.body: Gemini API keys are typed into the extension and stored in chrome.storage.local on your machine. Nothing is hardcoded in the source, so the repository can be pushed to GitHub without leaking a thing. When one key hits a rate limit, the pool rotates to the next one and carries on.
points: No key is shipped in the repository — the pool starts empty.
No analytics, no telemetry, no account, no sign-in.
Audio is held in IndexedDB on your device until you delete the take.
The only outward calls are to Gemini and LRCLIB, and only when you press the button.

faq.a: No. It captures the audio the tab is producing, through chrome.tabCapture. Your microphone is never opened, and your speakers stay unmuted.
Anything Chromium with the Side Panel API: Chrome, Edge, Brave and Opera, version 116 or newer.

faq.q: Do I need my own Gemini key?
faq.a: For transcription, yes — and it is free to make one in Google AI Studio. Paste one key or twenty; the extension rotates through them if one is rate limited. Keys stay in your browser's local storage.

faq.q: Can it handle Swahili and Sheng?
faq.a: That is what it was built for. Pick Kiswahili, English or auto-detect, and the transcription prompt is written to hold on to Swahili syllables, rhyme and code-switching.

faq.q: What happens if I close the popup mid-take?
faq.a: Nothing bad. A red REC badge stays on the toolbar icon and the offscreen recorder keeps going. Dock the studio with the pin button if you want a panel that cannot be dismissed by accident.

faq.q: Is it on the Chrome Web Store yet?
faq.a: Not yet — the listing is in review. Until then, download the .zip from the Install section: unzip it, drag the folder onto chrome://extensions, done in about thirty seconds. It is the same build Google is looking at.

faq.q: Why can I not just click a button and have it install?
faq.a: Because Chrome will not allow it. Google turned off website installs in 2022, for every developer, to stop extensions being pushed onto people. The two paths that exist are the Chrome Web Store — which is the one-click one, and is coming — and loading the folder yourself, which is the download above.

faq.q: What happens if I delete the folder after installing?
faq.a: The extension stops working and Chrome disables it. It reads the files from where you unzipped them, so the folder has to stay put. Put it somewhere you will not tidy away — Documents is a good home.

installSteps.title: Open chrome://extensions
installSteps.body: Download the .zip below and unzip it. You get one folder, tabtune-studio.

installSteps.title: Load unpacked
installSteps.body: Pick the TabTune Studio folder you cloned or unzipped.

installSteps.title: Pin it
installSteps.body: Puzzle icon, then pin TabTune Studio to the toolbar.

installSteps.title: Add a Gemini key
installSteps.body: Gear icon, paste one key per line, save. Recording works without it.

install.title: Download it, unzip it, drop it in
install.sub: Chrome stopped letting websites install extensions, so there is no one-click button — for us or for anybody else. What we can hand you is the folder itself. Unzip it, open chrome://extensions, drag the folder onto the page. That is the whole job, and it takes about thirty seconds.
install.fileNote: One .zip · about 83 kB · v1.2.0 · no account, no payment, no telemetry

steps.title: Unzip the download
steps.body: You get one folder, tabtune-studio. Leave it where it lands — Chrome reads it from there every time it starts, so deleting the folder turns the extension off.

steps.title: Open chrome://extensions
steps.body: Paste that into the address bar and hit enter. Flick the Developer mode switch in the top right. Identical in Edge, Brave, Opera and Vivaldi.

steps.title: Drag the folder onto that page
steps.body: The folder, not the zip. Chrome installs it the moment you let go — no dialog, no Load unpacked click. Pin it from the puzzle icon and you are done.

install.afterTitle: Nothing else is required, but two things help

after.label: Add a Gemini key
after.body: Only if you want transcription. Recording, karaoke and export all work without one. Make a key free at aistudio.google.com/apikey, paste it in the gear menu.

after.label: Learn one shortcut
after.body: Alt + Shift + R starts and stops a take from any tab, even with the panel closed. It is the one worth committing to memory.

permissions.title: Seven permissions, two hosts, and why
permissions.body: Anything that can record your audio has to ask for a lot, and Chrome shows the list before you install. Here it is in full, with the reason beside each one. If it is not on this list, TabTune Studio does not ask for it.

items.why: Records the audio the tab is already producing. Your microphone is never opened.
Keeps a take running after the panel closes, so a stray click cannot end it early.
Writes the .wav, the .lrc and the .zip bundle into your downloads folder.
Remembers your last ten takes and your Gemini keys, on your machine only.
Knows which tab you pressed record on, and stamps timestamps against it.
Lets the studio dock to the side of the window instead of living in a popup.
Sends audio to your own Gemini key when you ask for a transcription. Nothing is sent if you never press transcribe.
Fetches the synced lyrics you search for by hand. No listening history is shared with anyone.

permissions.footnote: No analytics, no advertising, no background network calls of any kind. The extension is quiet until you press a button.

plans.title: Free to record. Pro for the parts that cost money to run.
plans.sub: Everything that happens on your own machine is free and stays free: recording, editing, karaoke, export, and transcription through your own Gemini key. The line is a simple one — the moment a feature needs a server we have to pay for, it goes behind Pro.
plans.note: Pro is not on sale yet. Nothing on this site charges a card today; the shop takes orders over WhatsApp. This table is here so you can see where the line falls before you install, not to sell you something.
